thread:
liam: Quick bug report from sample-app onboarding. Our embed batching helper can scramble vector order when partial retries happen. Rerank consumer pairs vectors by index, so this causes wrong document scores.

nina: Which runtime/version? Node helper or sharedlib?

liam: Node, sample-app v2. The helper does concurrent chunk sends and on per-item retry it appends results to a flat array. If a retry resolves before another chunk finishes, ordering shifts.

raj: Can you paste the minimal flow? Even a sequence of events is fine.

liam: Sure. Start with items [d1,d2,d3,d4]. Chunks: [d1,d2] and [d3,d4]. If chunk2 has d4 timeout, we retry d4 solo. Responses arrive: chunk1 result, retry(d4), then chunk2 result(d3). Helper push order => [d1,d2,d4,d3]. Consumer expects [d1,d2,d3,d4].

nina: Sounds like the helper assumes FIFO arrival equals original order. Fix is to track original indices and write results into an output array at those indices.

raj: Agreed. Also possible mitigation: ask server to echo an id in each embedding response. But server currently returns flat arrays for perf. Helper should not depend on server echo.

liam: I put a small patch locally: when preparing requests we attach a transient mapping {local_req_id: original_index} and then, upon response, map each returned vector to its original slot. Works for both chunked and single-item retries.

nina: Nice. We should also add an opt-in SDK flag to set per-item idempotency headers so retries are deduped on the server when supported. That helps if a client accidentally double-sends the same item.

raj: Also add unit tests that introduce artificial delays and reorder responses to simulate races. We have flaky issues historically if tests don't assert strict ordering.

liam: Will open PR that: 1) implements index mapping in Node helper, 2) adds unit + integration rerank order test, 3) documents helper guarantees in sample-app README.

doc-bot: docs/embedding-ordering.md suggested: "helpers guarantee input-order; do not rely on server echo unless using echo_ids flag". Adding to onboarding checklist.

nina: After PR we should schedule a parity pass so Python/Rust helpers follow same semantics. IIRC Python already preserves order in retries but let's confirm.

raj: For long term, we might add a compact response envelope option server-side: return [{id, vector}] when requested. Add a small perf note that envelope adds ~8% payload overhead.

liam: Thanks all. Patching sample-app now and adding a short migration note for teams that assume positional pairing.

nina: Great catch. :metal:
